questions:
1. **Scope — which of the three proposed options ships?** The issue offers an "Italic" toggle in the properties panel, a Ctrl+I / Cmd+I shortcut, or a separate italic font. Suggested: an "Italic" toggle in the properties panel plus Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS); no separate italic font in the font list.
2. **Granularity — whole element or part of the text?** Suggested: italic is one property of the whole text element (like font family); there is no partial italic for selected words.
3. **Where the control appears and how it is labelled.** Suggested: an "Italic" toggle next to the text align control, tooltip "Italic (Ctrl+I)", shown when a text, a shape with text, an arrow with a label or a sticky note is selected, or the Text tool is active.
4. **Ctrl+I / Cmd+I details.** Suggested: toggles italic on the selected text(s) and on the text being edited (even when only part of it is highlighted in the editor); with nothing selected it does nothing; the browser's own Ctrl+I action (e.g. Firefox "Page Info") never opens while the canvas has focus; the existing single-key "I" tool shortcut is not triggered.
5. **Mixed selection.** Several texts selected, only some italic. Suggested: the toggle shows as not pressed; one click makes all italic, a second click removes italic from all.
6. **Default for new text.** Suggested: the last chosen italic value becomes the default for new text, like font family and size today.
7. **Fonts without a true italic face** (e.g. Hand-drawn/Excalifont, Code/Comic Shanns, and fonts in the full list). Suggested: every font can be made italic; where no italic face exists, a slanted (oblique) rendering is used; the canvas, the text editor and exports look the same.
8. **Layout effects.** Suggested: the selection box fits the slanted text and the last glyph's overhang is never clipped; text inside a shape re-wraps to the shape width and the shape grows taller if needed (width unchanged); an arrow label stays at the middle of the arrow; a sticky note's auto-fit takes italic into account and never shows the label larger than the picked size; while editing, the editor shows the text italic, so it does not jump when editing starts or ends.
9. **Scripts.** Suggested: italic applies to all scripts — Latin, Cyrillic, CJK, right-to-left (Arabic/Hebrew) and emoji — without clipping or crashes; RTL text slants as the browser renders it.
10. **Persistence, export and collaboration.** Suggested: italic survives a page reload, a saved .excalidraw file, PNG and SVG export, copy as PNG/SVG and live collaboration; an older Excalidraw version opens a file with italic text without error and shows it upright.
11. **Copies, styles and history.** Suggested: copy/paste styles, Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D, Alt+drag and library items carry italic; one italic toggle is undone with a single undo and restored with redo.
12. **Platforms.** Suggested: latest desktop Chrome, Firefox and Safari on Windows and macOS; the toggle also fits the mobile properties panel (375 px wide) without overlap.
answers:
Answers from the product owner, relayed by the user. Lines marked "(user)" are the product owner's words; lines marked "(accepted suggestion)" are suggested answers the user accepted with "For any question these do not cover, accept your suggested answer."

1. **Scope.** A panel toggle and Ctrl/Cmd+I; one italic property per text element, no separate font. (user)
2. **Granularity.** Whole element only. Bold is out of scope. (user)
3. **Control and label.** An "Italic" toggle next to the text align control, tooltip "Italic (Ctrl+I)", shown when a text, a shape with text, an arrow with a label or a sticky note is selected, or the Text tool is active. (accepted suggestion)
4. **Ctrl+I / Cmd+I.** Toggles italic on the selected text(s) and on the text being edited (even when only part of it is highlighted in the editor); with nothing selected it does nothing; the browser's own Ctrl+I action (e.g. Firefox "Page Info") never opens while the canvas has focus; the existing single-key "I" tool shortcut is not triggered. (accepted suggestion)
5. **Mixed selection.** With several texts selected and only some italic, the toggle shows as not pressed; one click makes all italic, a second click removes italic from all. (accepted suggestion)
6. **Default for new text.** The last italic value becomes the default for new text. (user)
7. **Fonts without a true italic face.** Synthetic oblique is allowed. (user) Every font can be made italic, and the canvas, the text editor and exports look the same. (accepted suggestion)
8. **Layout effects.** The selection box fits the slanted text and the last glyph's overhang is never clipped; text inside a shape re-wraps to the shape width and the shape grows taller if needed (width unchanged); an arrow label stays at the middle of the arrow; a sticky note's auto-fit takes italic into account and never shows the label larger than the picked size; while editing, the editor shows the text italic, so it does not jump when editing starts or ends. (accepted suggestion)
9. **Scripts.** Text stays readable and unclipped in Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew (right to left), emoji and mixed scripts; direction and alignment unchanged. (user)
10. **Persistence, export and collaboration.** Italic survives a page reload, a saved .excalidraw file, PNG and SVG export, copy as PNG/SVG and live collaboration; an older Excalidraw version opens a file with italic text without error and shows it upright. (accepted suggestion)
11. **Copies, styles and history.** Copy/paste styles, Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V, Ctrl+D, Alt+drag and library items carry italic; one italic toggle is undone with a single undo and restored with redo. (accepted suggestion) Color and opacity changes keep italic. (user)
12. **Platforms.** Latest desktop Chrome, Firefox and Safari on Windows and macOS; the toggle also fits the mobile properties panel (375 px wide) without overlap. (accepted suggestion)
